history.fact: About 95% of all Cava is made in the Penedès area of Catalonia.
Sant Sadurní d'Anoia is called the capital of Cava. Most Cava companies there can be visited.
In 1872, Josep Raventós made the first Cava in Spain using the traditional method, at Codorníu in Sant Sadurní d'Anoia. The provincial tourism site says the first batch was 3,000 bottles.

Traditional method means the bubbles come from a second fermentation inside the bottle. The bottles rest on their sides while this happens. The wine then ages on the dead yeast, which adds toasty and nutty notes over time.
The three classic grapes are Macabeo, Xarel·lo and Parellada. Chardonnay is also allowed. Allowed red grapes are Garnacha, Trepat, Pinot Noir and Monastrell, mostly used for rosé.

Aging tiers (minimum time on the yeast): Cava de Guarda 9 months; Reserva more than 18 months; Gran Reserva 30 months; Cava de Paraje Calificado (single site) more than 36 months. Gran Reserva and Paraje Calificado must be dry (Brut Nature, Extra Brut or Brut).
Phylloxera, a vine pest, wrecked Penedès vineyards in the late 1800s. Growers replanted with native white grapes, which helped Cava grow.
'Cava' means 'cave' or 'cellar' in Spanish. Wine was aged in underground cellars. Spanish makers adopted the name officially around 1970 to set their wine apart from French Champagne.

The split, in plain terms: some top family wineries felt the Cava name had become tied to cheap wine. Raventós i Blanc left the Cava DO in 2012. Clàssic Penedès formed in 2013 under the Penedès DO, with 100% organic grapes. In January 2019, six wineries including Gramona, Recaredo, Llopart and Torelló left to form Corpinnat. Corpinnat requires organic grapes, local varieties, a set minimum grape price and at least 18 months of aging. These wines no longer say 'Cava' on the label.
In March 2026, Juvé & Camps voted to leave the Cava DO and join Corpinnat. It became the group's 22nd winery and largest member.

region.summary: Penedès sits about halfway between Barcelona and Tarragona, roughly 42 km from each. Inland it is a wide valley of vineyards. Montserrat's jagged peaks rise to the north, and some wineries, like Llopart, have vineyard views to the mountain. Sant Sadurní d'Anoia is in the Alt Penedès county, on the R4 train line and the AP-7 highway.

getting_there.cost: Not confirmed for 2026. One guide lists €6.90 each way. A 10-trip Bonotren card for 3 zones costs €27.60 (zone for Sant Sadurní not confirmed).
getting_there.notes: Board at Plaça de Catalunya, Arc de Triomf or Barcelona-Sants. Trains run about every 30 to 60 minutes on weekdays. Freixenet is right across from Sant Sadurní station. Codorníu is about 1.5 km away. The R4 has frequent delays, so build in a buffer. The Martorell to Sant Sadurní stretch was closed after a fatal wall collapse at Gelida on January 20, 2026, and reopened April 7, 2026. Free Rodalies travel ended May 9, 2026.

glossary.meaning: Driest. 0-3 grams of sugar per liter, no sugar added.
Dry, the most common style. Up to 12 g/L sugar.
Lightly sweet, despite the name ('dry'). 17-32 g/L.
Rosé Cava. Made the same way, often with red grapes like Garnacha, Trepat, Pinot Noir or Monastrell.
Entry tier, at least 9 months of aging.
Aged at least 30 months. Always dry.
Single named site, aged more than 36 months. Top tier.
Label used by top Penedès wineries that left the Cava DO. Organic, local grapes, at least 18 months aging.
